Section 3 • Transmitted Flux

3.5 Transmission and Flux

It is useful to distinguish between transmission, \(T(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda)\), and flux, \(F(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda)\). The transmission is the dimensionless attenuation factor produced by absorption alone, whereas the observed flux is obtained by multiplying that attenuation by the emitted continuum, \(F_0(\Lambda)\). This distinction is especially helpful when several transitions contribute simultaneously, since optical depths add while transmission factors multiply.

In the straight-line approximation introduced in Sec. 3.4, the optical depth depends on both the spectral coordinate \(\Lambda\) and the transverse comoving position \(\vec{x}_{\perp}\) that labels the sightline. Accordingly, the transmitted flux and the transmission factor associated with transition \(j\) of species \(i\) are \begin{equation} F_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) = F_0(\Lambda)\, T_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right), \qquad T_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) \coloneqq \exp\!\left[-\tau_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\right]. \tag{3.23} \end{equation}

If several transitions contribute to the absorption, the total optical depth is the sum of the individual optical depths. Therefore, the total transmission along the sightline \(\vec{x}_{\perp}\) is \begin{align} T\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) &= \exp\!\left[-\tau\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\right] = \exp\!\left[-\sum_{\{i,j\}}\tau_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\right] = \prod_{\{i,j\}}T_{ij}\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right). \tag{3.24} \end{align} The total transmitted flux is then \begin{align} F\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) = F_0(\Lambda)\,T\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right) = F_0(\Lambda)\exp\!\left[-\tau\!\left(\vec{x}_{\perp},\Lambda\right)\right]. \tag{3.25} \end{align}
